scope.locator_convention: Accepted-view OOXML; one-based top-level paragraph/table and unique physical-cell row/column coordinates. Merged cells are not expanded into duplicate grid cells.
scope.digit_inventory_rule: Original cells containing ASCII digits; complete table structures additionally retain labels with Unicode-only subscripts.
scope.numerical_value_policy: All scientific values are selected from validated aggregate results. Contextual age thresholds, interval levels and enrollment dates are labels, not estimates.
scope.interval_policy: Point estimator, unit, interval type and support remain source-specific; stochastic rounding differences do not add an acceptance gate.
scope.unavailable_policy: Null input facts are explicitly unavailable, never zero, suppressed or replaced with manuscript literals.

sentences.template: Among {cohort} children with eligible spirometry or oscillometry, {early} had TB before age five, including {infancy} during infancy.
Pre- and post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC were available for {pre} and {post} children.

Compared with the modelled no-prior-TB state, pre-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC differences after TB before age five and infancy TB were {before_five} and {infancy} percentage points, respectively (posterior mean and 95% credible interval).
Corresponding post-bronchodilator differences were {before_five} and {infancy} percentage points, respectively (posterior mean and 95% credible interval).
The adjusted standardized risk ratio for current wheeze following infancy TB at ages one to younger than three years was {early} (posterior median and 95% credible interval).
sentences.notes: Standardized risk ratio, not the conditional odds ratio.

sentences.template: For enrollment between March 5, 2012, and March 31, 2015, antenatal enrollment and combined antenatal follow-up or pregnancy losses cannot be reconstructed from the supplied inputs ({enrollment} and {losses}, respectively); {women} women had {children} liveborn children (twin pairs: {twins}; triplet sets: {triplets}; Figure S1).
sentences.notes: Enrollment dates are manuscript context. The two unavailable quantities remain explicit null states; no missing component is treated as zero or filled from a literal manuscript number.

sentences.template: Of these children, {pft} contributed at least one lung-function measurement, and {cohort} had at least one eligible spirometry or oscillometry measurement and comprised the combined cohort described in Table 1.
The expanded joint models retained all {joint} children across the available longitudinal and first-TB processes.

The overlapping outcome-specific samples included {pre} children contributing pre-bronchodilator spirometry and up to {post} contributing post-bronchodilator spirometry to the expanded joint models, {mechanics} with respiratory-mechanics measurements, and {within_breath} with within-breath oscillometry measurements, including {reactance} with low-frequency reactance.
sentences.notes: The post-bronchodilator maximum is the FVC native model; the FEV₁/FVC sample is separately reported.

sentences.template: Among the {cohort} children, {early} ({percent}%) had a first TB episode before age five years.

The median age at first TB was {age} years (median [IQR]); {infancy} children ({infancy_percent}%) experienced TB during infancy and {older} ({older_percent}%) from age one to younger than five years.
Of the {no_early} children without TB before age five, {never} had no recorded TB and {later} first developed TB at age five years or older (Figure S1).

Children with early-childhood TB and those without TB before age five had Mbekweni recruitment proportions of {mbekweni_early}% and {mbekweni_reference}%, Black African ethnicity proportions of {black_early}% and {black_reference}%, mean birthweights of {birthweight_early} and {birthweight_reference} g, and maternal smoking exposure proportions of {smoking_early}% and {smoking_reference}%, respectively (Table 1).

In expanded shared-parameter joint models retaining measurements after TB at any recorded age, pre-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC differences following TB before age five and infancy TB were {before_five} and {infancy} percentage points, respectively (posterior mean and 95% CrI; Table 2; Figure 2).
Corresponding GLI z-score differences were {before_five} and {infancy}, respectively (posterior mean and 95% CrI).
Mean FEV₁ and FVC differences following TB before age five or during infancy remained uncertain (Table 2).

sentences.template: The trajectory analysis included {measurements} measurements from {children} children.

For predicted FEV₁/FVC trajectories between ages five and ten years, TB-by-age interaction p values on the percentage and GLI z-score scales were {native_infancy} and {z_infancy}, respectively, for infancy TB, and {native_early} and {z_early}, respectively, for TB before age five (Figure 1).
sentences.notes: Raw three-degree-of-freedom interaction Wald p values from full models; neither the overall four-degree-of-freedom test nor multiplicity-adjusted p values.

sentences.template: In reduced models without interaction terms, average differences across the age range were {infancy} percentage points following infancy TB and {before_five} percentage points following TB before age five (estimate and 95% CI).
Corresponding average GLI z-score differences were {infancy} and {before_five}, respectively (estimate and 95% CI).
Analyses of spirometric indices below the lower limit of normal and abnormal patterns at ages five to ten years included up to {measurements} measurements from {children} children.
sentences.notes: The maximum eligible pre-bronchodilator binary outcome sample; outcome-specific complete-case counts remain distinct.

sentences.template: In repeated-measures modified Poisson models of pre-bronchodilator outcomes, adjusted risk ratios following infancy TB were {ratio} for FEV₁/FVC below the lower limit of normal, {fev} for FEV₁ below the lower limit of normal, and {obstruction} for an obstructive spirometric pattern (estimate and 95% CI; Figure 2).
For TB occurring before age five, adjusted risk ratios were {ratio} for FEV₁/FVC below the lower limit of normal and {obstruction} for obstruction (estimate and 95% CI).
Post-bronchodilator estimates for FEV₁/FVC below the lower limit of normal and an obstructive pattern were imprecise and compatible with no association (Figure 2).

sentences.notes: The calendar restriction is an analysis-configuration input, not a hardcoded reporting date. Both restricted all-age and restricted early-TB models remain distinct.

sentences.template: In sensitivity analyses of the early-TB specification, simultaneous adjustment for maternal HIV, prenatal maternal smoking and birthweight yielded differences of {before_five} and {infancy} percentage points (posterior mean and 95% CrI); exploratory adjustment for ever-recorded lower respiratory tract infection was also evaluated (Tables S1 and S3).
sentences.notes: LRTI adjustment is exploratory; LRTI does not enter the first-TB baseline hazard. Birthweight availability changes the eligible sample.
